claims.text: An optimized lightweight high-entropy alloy composition can combine low density, mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The combined properties arise when the optimized composition promotes a continuous, nanostructured passivating oxide layer and a refined, distortion-hardened microstructure.
The initial alloy has a predominantly single-phase, homogeneous microstructure.
The optimized composition produces significant lattice distortion.
Composition-induced lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion enhances the alloy's mechanical strength.
The optimized composition drives formation of a coherent, protective oxide layer.
A coherent protective oxide layer reduces corrosive and oxidative degradation.
The full-concentration alloy will have statistically significantly higher yield strength than an alloy with reduced oxide-former content.
The full-concentration alloy will have a lower corrosion rate than the reduced-content baseline.
The full-concentration alloy will have a lower oxidation rate than the reduced-content baseline.
The full-concentration alloy will exhibit a uniform, adherent passivation layer.
Temperatures above the oxide layer's stability range can coarsen or disrupt the protective oxide scale.
Conditions that induce phase segregation can eliminate the uniform microstructure and cause the hypothesized property combination to cease.
Variations in alloy processing and testing conditions can affect the magnitude of the anticipated benefits.
Failure to obtain statistically significant strength improvements and lower corrosion and oxidation rates relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a uniform, nanostructured passivating oxide layer would falsify the hypothesis.
